newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Long Australian bond yields off awaiting budget.
newsitem.headline: Long Australian bond yields off awaiting budget.

text.p: *Long-dated Australian bond yields edged to their lowest level since late February in early trading in the wake of a firmer bias in U.S. debt and ahead of the Federal budget.
*1997/98 budget to be handed down at 7.30 p.m. (0930 GMT).
Long-dated Australian bond yields edged to their lowest level since late February in early trading in the wake of a firmer bias in U.S. Treasuries on Monday and ahead of the Federal budget.

The June 10-year bond futures contract struck a high of 92.350 just after the opening, taking the benchmark 10-year bond yield down to around 7.60 percent, but slipped back slightly in fairly slow turnover.
"Physicals are quiet, futures are quiet. It looks as if the market is going to be pretty much on hold going into the budget," one trader said.
"Even after the budget, I'm not sure that we are going to get too carried away. We're not expecting any surprises. It's a fairly laid back affair this time round," he added.

However, the 1997/98 budget is expected to be positive for the market with a substantial headline surplus expected after the recent airport sales and taking into account the part sale of Telstra, lessening the need for bond issuance next fiscal year. Treasurer Peter Costello is due to hand down the government's second budget at 7.30 p.m. (0930 GMT).
The Sydney Futures Exchange will be open for a special budget session between 7.00 p.m. to 8.15 p.m. (0900-1015 GMT).

Long dated bonds slightly outperformed the U.S., which succumbed to profit-taking into the run-up to the New York close, but showed a firmer bias in anticipation of weak data for retail sales later on Tuesday and subdued inflation reports later in the week.
